hillClimb.unitOfChange: one bounded hypothesis targeting one failing criterion
acceptWhen: all previously passing hard gates remain passing
the lexicographic objective improves or stays equal with lower complexity
rejectWhen: a score rises by deleting evidence, caveats, credits, or accessibility affordances
a human approval is guessed or self-certified by an agent
the change improves only the grader-facing wording rather than the reader experience
the change introduces an unrelated redesign or broad refactor
stopWhen: the suite target is reached in the required consecutive independent runs
the next failing item requires human approval or rights clearance
three bounded attempts fail to improve the same criterion
the proposed improvement conflicts with a protected invariant

rubric.0.8: All three priority cases show relevant artifacts with captions and public-safe boundaries, and at least two artifacts reveal Jamie's actual work product.
rubric.1: All three show decisive work-product artifacts that materially improve understanding, with verified rights, alt text, and mobile legibility.

antiGaming: A colored text card labeled artifact is not an artifact.
Do not publish an unapproved private image.
Do not use representative imagery as direct proof of a specific event.

criteria.name: A hiring reader can identify role, value, proof, and next action
criteria.intent: The site should minimize the reader's burden without flattening the record.
evidence: KC Town Hall opening and working-neighborhood-interface section
criteria.passCondition: Within a 30-second skim, an independent grader can state Jamie's target role, recurring contribution, two concrete proofs, and the next action without consulting source notes.

rubric.0.5: Role is clear but proof or next action requires deep reading.
rubric.0.8: Role, value, two proofs, and next action are clear in a short skim.
rubric.1: The path is immediate, memorable, specific, and free of avoidable repetition.

antiGaming: Do not replace specific proof with generic leadership language.
Do not optimize only for keyword density.
Do not remove necessary collective-credit qualifiers.

criteria.name: Priority surfaces pass Chad's lens
criteria.intent: The portfolio should make Jamie's specific contribution, purpose, and usable result legible without asking a hiring or public-sector reader to decode domain language or evidence governance.
evidence: HJE, FairRentNYC, and CallNYC case-study openings
KC Town Hall opening and working-neighborhood-interface section
criteria.passCondition: In one pass, two independent graders can identify Jamie as the actor, describe the concrete work he performed, name what became usable and toward what end, and distinguish his contribution from collective outcomes on the homepage, Technical Operations page, resume, at least two priority case studies, and KC Town Hall.

rubric.0: Jamie is hidden behind projects, abstractions, or unexplained domain language.
rubric.0.5: Jamie is visible, but the work product, purpose, or usable change must be inferred on several priority surfaces.
rubric.0.8: The actor, concrete intervention, usable result, and purpose are clear in one pass across the required surfaces, with collective work accurately bounded.
rubric.1: Every priority surface gives an immediate, specific, memorable account of Jamie's intervention and its value without avoidable abstraction, repetition, or reader-facing process language.

antiGaming: Do not insert Jamie or I mechanically without naming a concrete action and usable result.
Do not delete collective-credit, uncertainty, source, or public-safety qualifiers.
Do not add rubric-facing phrases such as for a hiring manager merely to explain relevance.
Do not strengthen causality, ownership, authority, or outcome claims beyond the knowledge bank.

criteria.name: Knowledge maturity matches the work actually performed
criteria.intent: The bank should distinguish captured metadata from close-read evidence, and close-read evidence from editorially selected public claims.
evidence: all metadata-reviewed and decomposed public intake records
their linked atomic claim candidates, evidence relationships, and locators
their doesNotEstablish boundaries and research inquiries
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders find that every decomposed source yields specific atomic propositions, evidence roles, locators, and limits, while metadata-reviewed sources remain claim-free, unsurfaced, and queued for selective close reading.

rubric.0: Sources are stored only as links or converted directly into broad promotional claims.
rubric.0.5: Some claims are decomposed, but maturity states are inflated or support, attribution, collective credit, and limitations remain conflated.
rubric.0.8: Every decomposed source has useful atomic knowledge and boundaries; metadata-only sources remain visibly staged with a next action and no claim or projection edge.
rubric.1: Maturity is consistently truthful across intake, source, claim, evidence, inquiry, and editorial layers, making both deep evidence and undecomposed research queues immediately legible.

antiGaming: Do not create many near-duplicate assertions merely to increase apparent depth.
Do not mark a source decomposed merely because its title, URL, and campaign placement were recovered.
Do not convert Jamie's memory into independent corroboration.
Do not let movement coverage establish sole causality or authorship.
Do not quote or reproduce copyrighted source text beyond the minimum needed for identification.

criteria.name: Case studies preserve nuance without evidence-dump repetition
criteria.intent: Public prose stays primary while citations, care notes, and governance remain available at the right depth.
evidence: HJE, FairRentNYC, CallNYC, KC Town Hall, and Source-Backed Team Memory pages
criteria.passCondition: The opening communicates role, action, outcome, and artifact; later governance sections add new information rather than restating the same boundary.

rubric.0: The page reads as a database or internal governance dump.
rubric.0.5: The story is credible but substantially repetitive.
rubric.0.8: The narrative is composed, skimmable, and appropriately layered.
rubric.1: Every section earns its place and evidence depth never displaces the reader's story.

antiGaming: Do not delete source limitations to make the page shorter.
Do not move private governance language into public prose.
Do not hide required disclaimers in inaccessible interactions.

criteria.name: The site sounds warm, precise, useful, and human
criteria.intent: Jamie should remain visible as a careful systems-builder rather than becoming generic portfolio copy.
evidence: homepage, About, Contact, priority case-study prose, and KC Town Hall
Jamie's writer's-voice guide used only as an editorial reference
criteria.passCondition: The prose joins care to structure, distinguishes known from assumed, uses active specific language, and ends in a usable next step.

rubric.0.5: Accurate but flat or overly procedural.
rubric.0.8: Warm, precise, modular, and clearly Jamie's.
rubric.1: Distinctive voice improves trust and action without ornament or overclaiming.

antiGaming: Do not imitate private writing or publish private details.
Do not add lyrical language where plain operational language is clearer.
Do not use first-person warmth to blur collective credit.

criteria.name: The portfolio preserves embodied artistic and relational intelligence
criteria.intent: Hiring clarity should not flatten Jamie's artistic, hospitable, spatial, and relational practice into conventional administration or treat organizational utility as the only form of value.
evidence: at least two public case studies spanning cultural, civic, or technical work
the public-safe Open House claim and its published source
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders find a visible, source-backed threshold connecting artistic, civic, technical, and social practice; at least one public passage shows how participation, place, hospitality, atmosphere, or embodied inquiry changes the character of Jamie's operating work; and no protected educational record, private correspondence, or unapproved testimonial is exposed.

rubric.0: The portfolio reduces Jamie to generic administration or uses protected educational and relationship material as public endorsement.
rubric.0.5: Artistic and relational history is mentioned, but it reads as an unrelated prehistory or does not change how the present practice is understood.
rubric.0.8: A concise public-safe passage connects embodied, artistic, relational, spatial, and operational practice while preserving source, consent, and collective-credit boundaries.
rubric.1: The connection is memorable and necessary to the professional argument: readers understand why Jamie's systems attend to participation, memory, place, atmosphere, and how people inhabit structures without losing role clarity.

antiGaming: Do not publish grades, scores, student identifiers, full narrative evaluations, private correspondence, or an unapproved recommendation.
Do not add decorative art language that has no source-backed relationship to Jamie's practice.
Do not weaken role clarity or claim every project is an artwork merely to satisfy the lens.
Do not erase collaborators, residents, participants, or shared authorship from participatory work.

criteria.name: The portfolio reveals recursive social-systems and prototyping intelligence
criteria.intent: The public argument should make visible the longstanding practice of studying relationships recursively, building prototypes, and joining physical and digital participation rather than presenting later operating structure as a generic management technique.
evidence: WOW List, CallNYC, and Source-Backed Team Memory public narratives
the public-safe Open House claim and its published source
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders can identify a credible lineage from participatory or social-software experiments to current systems work, including relationships made visible, a tested interface or prototype, and a physical or social context people can inhabit, without inflating protected coursework into present-day production machine-learning or social-network-analysis expertise.

rubric.0: The portfolio presents only generic project management or makes inflated technical claims from protected coursework.
rubric.0.5: Systems and prototypes are visible, but the recursive social and physical-digital lineage remains implicit or disconnected from current work.
rubric.0.8: The portfolio clearly connects early participatory systems thinking to current interfaces, workflows, prototypes, and source-backed knowledge systems with accurate technical and collective boundaries.
rubric.1: Readers can see a distinctive, continuous method: Jamie studies relationships, prototypes a representation or interface, and makes a social system more perceivable and actionable across physical and digital settings.

antiGaming: Do not claim Jamie invented structural equivalence or convert a professor's historical assessment into field-wide priority.
Do not present collective student design as Jamie's sole authorship.
Do not infer current production AI, computer-vision, or social-network-analysis capability from 2004-2006 course work.
Do not add technical vocabulary unless a public reader can see the system, relationship, interface, or use it describes.

criteria.name: Public projection selects a memorable argument from the deeper bank
criteria.intent: The public portfolio should use the knowledge bank's depth to make deliberate choices, not reproduce archival completeness or ask the reader to choose among every available proof.
evidence: homepage Start here section and featured work
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders find one coherent role argument, no more than four primary proof examples on the Technical Operations opening path, and a visible distinction between selected public proof and the larger retained archive.

rubric.0: The public experience reproduces the archive or offers an undifferentiated project inventory.
rubric.0.5: A role argument exists, but priority surfaces still ask the reader to process too many equivalent examples.
rubric.0.8: The role argument and a small complementary proof set are clear while deeper material remains available elsewhere.
rubric.1: Every visible proof earns its place, reinforces a distinct part of the argument, and leaves a concise memorable account.

antiGaming: Do not delete knowledge-bank depth to make the public site shorter.
Do not hide weak selection behind generic category labels.
Do not choose only the most impressive-looking project when another offers stronger role evidence.

criteria.name: Unprimed hiring readers understand, trust, remember, and act
criteria.intent: Actual hiring-reader behavior should test the portfolio beyond LLM judgments of prose quality and rubric compliance.
evidence: at least five coded, unprimed 30-second reader sessions using evals/launch-readiness/v24/reader-study-template.json
aggregate recall, trust, role-fit, and next-action findings without participant identities or raw private comments
criteria.passCondition: At least four of five unprimed target readers correctly state Jamie's role, recurring contribution, two concrete proofs, and next action; no repeated trust or comprehension failure remains unresolved.

rubric.0: No unprimed human reader study exists, or most readers cannot identify Jamie's role and value.
rubric.0.5: Readers understand the role but recall little proof, report avoidable mistrust, or cannot identify the next action.
rubric.0.8: At least four of five readers meet the complete recall-and-action task with no critical trust failure.
rubric.1: Readers independently converge on the intended role, contribution, complementary proofs, and next action in language close to the portfolio's intended argument.

antiGaming: An agent may prepare the study but may not impersonate human readers or fabricate observations.
Do not prime participants with the target answer or explain the site before the timed task.
Do not commit participant identities, recordings, or raw private feedback.

criteria.name: Archive visibility does not become a proxy for professional importance
criteria.intent: The system should notice quiet facilitation, maintenance, failed experiments, conflict repair, and less-digitized collaboration instead of allowing abundant platform traces to dominate professional history.
evidence: knowledge-bank research inquiries and source-class distribution
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders find that the archive-bias audit names underrepresented labor and evidence classes, routes each to a bounded research or collaborator-review action, and prevents source abundance or social metrics from determining public importance.

rubric.0: Recoverable digital volume is implicitly treated as importance or impact.
rubric.0.5: Archive bias is acknowledged but not connected to research, editorial, or collaborator-review actions.
rubric.0.8: Major underrepresented labor categories have explicit mitigation and do not distort public selection.
rubric.1: Selection decisions demonstrably balance source quality, role relevance, consequence, and missing-record awareness across projects.

antiGaming: Do not invent invisible labor merely to balance the archive.
Do not downgrade well-supported work because it has abundant records.
Do not turn first-person memory into independent corroboration.

criteria.name: Case studies distinguish action, output, use, and bounded consequence
criteria.intent: The portfolio should explain why work mattered while preserving the difference between Jamie's intervention, a produced artifact, observed use, institutional action, and collective outcome.
evidence: priority case-study openings and outcome sections
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders can classify each priority case's action, output, observed use, and strongest bounded consequence without finding sole-causality, adoption, reach, or impact inflation.

rubric.0: Activity is presented as impact or collective outcomes are assigned to Jamie.
rubric.0.5: Actions and outputs are clear, but use or consequence is vague, absent, or conflated with causality.
rubric.0.8: Priority cases communicate a specific bounded consequence and preserve evidence and collective-credit limits.
rubric.1: The portfolio makes consequence memorable and decision-relevant while every causal boundary remains immediately intelligible.

antiGaming: Do not replace consequence with unsupported reach, engagement, or policy-causality language.
Do not soften every outcome into meaninglessness merely to avoid risk.
Do not infer current adoption from historical availability.

criteria.name: Historical work resolves into a credible present and future contribution
criteria.intent: Deep civic, cultural, and business histories should make Jamie's current Technical Project Management, implementation, product operations, knowledge-system, and AI-evaluation capabilities easier to understand.
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders can name the roles and operating environments Jamie is prepared to enter now, connect at least three historical examples to current capabilities, and identify a credible next contribution without generic future-potential language.

rubric.0: The portfolio reads mainly as an archive of past civic and cultural projects.
rubric.0.5: The target role is named, but the bridge from past work to current contribution remains implicit or generic.
rubric.0.8: Present role fit and three evidence-backed capability bridges are explicit and credible.
rubric.1: The historical range feels necessary to a distinctive, immediately useful present-tense offer and a plausible next chapter.

antiGaming: Do not imply current expertise unsupported by the project record or recent learning.
Do not recast every historical project in fashionable terminology.
Do not hide dates or make dormant projects appear currently active.

criteria.name: Collaborator review can confirm social truth without becoming testimonial theater
criteria.intent: Where role division or consequence depends on lived collaboration, the portfolio should invite correction and permission without pressuring collaborators or converting archive research into eyewitness testimony.
evidence: approval register entries for any collaborator-sensitive public claim or asset
criteria.passCondition: Every priority collaborator-sensitive claim has an approved, corrected, declined, unreachable, or omitted disposition; any public quotation, testimonial, photograph, or strengthened role claim has explicit human permission.

rubric.0: Collaborator-sensitive claims are projected without review, or AI archival notes are presented as testimony.
rubric.0.5: A review process exists but important role or permission questions remain unresolved on public surfaces.
rubric.0.8: Priority claims have explicit dispositions and unresolved material is held or omitted.
rubric.1: Collaborator review materially improves accuracy and credit while preserving consent, disagreement, and nonresponse as legitimate outcomes.

antiGaming: An agent may prepare review materials but may not provide collaborator consent or approval.
Do not treat silence, a public relationship, or prior collaboration as permission.
Do not commit private replies, contact details, or interpersonal context.

criteria.name: An evaluator outside the rubric identifies omitted failure modes
criteria.intent: The system should resist Goodharting by asking an independent evaluator who did not author the rubric to identify important failures the known criteria do not reward or penalize.
evidence: a disposition for every material omitted-risk finding
a record of accepted, rejected, duplicate, and deferred rubric changes
criteria.passCondition: At least one independent human evaluator, without seeing the criterion list before review, inspects the portfolio and names omitted risks; every material finding receives a reasoned disposition and accepted gaps become versioned criteria.

rubric.0: No holdout audit exists, or the evaluator was primed with the rubric and merely repeated it.
rubric.0.5: A holdout review exists but findings lack disposition or do not influence the system.
rubric.0.8: The unprimed review produces reasoned dispositions and no material omitted failure remains untracked.
rubric.1: Repeated holdout reviews discover diminishing material omissions while keeping the suite smaller and more discriminating.

antiGaming: An agent may prepare the audit but may not impersonate an independent human holdout evaluator.
Do not show the evaluator the rubric before the open-ended review.
Do not add every suggestion as a criterion without deduplication and materiality review.

criteria.name: The knowledge and evaluation system remains operable as it grows
criteria.intent: Repository depth should not create an unreviewable maintenance burden, duplicate truth stores, stale current-version pointers, or a process only its authors can operate.
evidence: AGENTS.md current-version pointer and repository commands
canonical knowledge-intake and citation validation paths
criteria.passCondition: Two independent graders can identify one current suite, one canonical claim path, one intake workflow, and one release command; the maintenance scorecard records growth risks, pruning rules, stale-review handling, and a bounded update budget.

rubric.0: Multiple competing truth stores or undocumented procedures make safe updates impractical.
rubric.0.5: The system is documented but version growth, duplicate checks, or manual review burden remain uncontrolled.
rubric.0.8: Current ownership, canonical paths, commands, pruning, and stale-review policies are explicit and usable by a new contributor.
rubric.1: The system's trust and coverage grow without proportional process burden, and obsolete machinery is deliberately retired rather than accumulated.

antiGaming: Do not delete historical eval versions or evidence needed for auditability.
Do not call the system maintainable merely because checks pass on one machine.
Do not create a second canonical knowledge store to simplify one task.

criteria.name: Production release preserves staging safety and production indexability
criteria.intent: The canonical domain should serve the reviewed portfolio with environment-correct metadata and a reversible deployment.
evidence: production /api/health, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, canonical metadata, social image, and resume PDF
criteria.passCondition: The exact reviewed SHA passes production preflight; jamieburk.art serves the new app; production is indexable; staging remains noindex; all canonical routes and the PDF return 200; rollback is documented.
antiGaming: Do not make staging indexable.
Do not mark the gate passed from a local build alone.
Do not redirect the canonical domain to the legacy application.

criteria.name: Required public-use and launch approvals are explicit
criteria.intent: Publication permission remains distinct from evidence availability.
evidence: human approval record tied to the reviewed commit
criteria.passCondition: Jamie explicitly approves the final resume, phone-in-PDF behavior, public metrics, collaborator-sensitive assets, and production deployment; approval and blocker records agree.
antiGaming: An agent may report this gate but may not approve it.
A merged branch is not publication consent.
Public availability is not rights clearance.

criteria.name: The application handoff is small and role-specific
criteria.intent: A job application should send a purposeful route through the portfolio rather than the entire archive.
criteria.passCondition: For a named role, the application packet contains the resume, homepage or Technical Operations page, and no more than two cases whose relevance can be explained in one sentence each.

rubric.0.5: The packet exists but is generic or overloaded.
rubric.0.8: The packet is concise, role-specific, and uses the canonical production domain.
rubric.1: The packet anticipates the role's operating needs and every included link earns its place.

antiGaming: An agent may propose the packet, but the final role-specific selection requires human review.
Do not create a new landing page for every application.
Do not include more cases merely to look comprehensive.
Do not use staging URLs in a final external application unless explicitly necessary.
